excerpt: The Agriculture, Food, and Natural Resources (AFNR) Career Cluster focuses on the essential elements of life food, water, land, and air. This career cluster includes a diverse spectrum of occupations, ranging from farmer, rancher, and veterinarian to geologist, land conservation.

Agribusiness
Animal Science
Applied Agricultural Engineering
Environmental and Natural Resources
Food Science and Technology
Plant Science
*Optional Use the web diagram template so that students can define the career pathways.

Definition of Agriculture

Agriculture is a science, art, or practice of cultivating the soil, producing crops, and raising livestock and in varying degrees the preparation and marketing of the resulting products Today we will focus on the plant science side of agriculture.
How do we grow Plants? Write it down on a Sticky note then place inside the tree.

Plant Science

The Plant Science program of study focuses on the science, research, and business of plants and other living organisms. It teaches students how to apply biology and life science to real-world life processes of plants and vegetation, either in laboratories or in the field.

Careers in plant science:

Horticulture
Floral Design
Forestry
Turf Management
Viticulture
Soil Science
Let's break them down and find out what each career does. Please take out your Plant Systems Career Pathways Note Sheet

Plant Science is split in two sections:

Horticulture is the science of producing, processing, and marketing fruits (pomology), vegetables (olericulture) and ornamental plants.

Floral Design or Floriculture is an area of Ornamental horticulture that includes the production, transportation, and use of cut flowers and foliage and of greenhouse crops.

What are 3 things they have in common?

Soil
Water
Sunlight
Soil is a common factor. What is soil? Is it dirt???

Soil is not dirt…….it’s much more!

Soil contains minerals, air, water and organic matter. Combine that with some sun and we are able to grow life!

Most of our FOOD comes from plants in the SOIL. Part of the OXYGEN we breathe comes from plants. Most of the WATER we drink and use is cleaned by SOIL. These are all factors that contribute to soil.

Lab Activity

Let’s check out what is in our soil on our campus.
Please take out your Let’s Find Out About Soil handout.
You will need the following items:
1 spoon
1 ziplock sandwich baggie
We will go outside and fill our bags ⅓ of the way full. Please make sure you take soil samples where the soil is soft and not hard. It could break your spoon.

After our soil collection

Place your bag flat on the table so that the soil can take up most of the bag. Do not open the bag, you will feel and see your soil through the ziplock bag. Please answer the questions on your Let’s Find Out About Soil handout.

Extend Activity
Extend: (20-30 Minutes)
Students will complete the soil lab. Instructor will take students outside to an area where there is visible soft soil. Students will be able to fill their bag ⅓ of the way up. Students will use their spoons to act like shovels. Once collection of soil is over, bring the students back inside and instruct them to lay their bags flat on the desk. The soil should take up all of the space in their bag and the student can have a better look at their soil and answer the questions on their Let’s Find Out About Soil handout.

To dispose of soil you can take students to empty them together at once or have a bucket where students can dispose of it and then take it outside back in the environment at the conclusion of this lesson.
